tool_input.content:
Incident: KubePodCrashLooping, namespace shop, cluster aurora-lab (kind-aurora-lab via kubeconfig agent).

Root cause: ConfigMap `frontend-nginx` (mounted at /etc/nginx/conf.d in the `frontend` Deployment) contained an nginx directive typo: `proxy_conect_timeout` instead of `proxy_connect_timeout`. nginx fails to start with `[emerg] unknown directive` and exits code 1, causing CrashLoopBackOff.

Key mechanism: ConfigMap is referenced by plain name (not hash-suffixed/immutable), so it's shared across all ReplicaSet revisions of the Deployment. Pods that were already running before the bad config was written kept serving fine (nginx doesn't hot-reload conf.d). The crash only became visible when a `kubectl rollout restart` created NEW pods that mounted the already-broken ConfigMap for the first time. Service endpoints still only included the healthy old pods, so this presented as a *partial* degradation (1/3 replicas unavailable), not a full outage — but it meant there was no healthy replacement available if the old pods were ever cycled.

**How to apply next time a similar alert fires:**
1. `kubectl get pods -n <ns> -o wide` — look for multiple ReplicaSets of the same deployment; if only the newest RS is crashing while an older RS is healthy, suspect a config/env change exposed by a recent rollout/restart, not a code bug.
2. `kubectl logs <crashing-pod>` first — config parse errors show up immediately and are definitive.
3. Diff the ConfigMap/Secret referenced by the pod against what the healthy old pods would have had — since ConfigMaps aren't versioned by default, check `kubectl describe configmap` content directly for typos/syntax errors.
4. Fix is to correct the ConfigMap content, NOT `rollout undo` — rollback doesn't help if the ConfigMap is shared by name across revisions.
5. Check `kubectl get endpoints <svc>` to assess real user impact before escalating severity — if old healthy pods are still in the endpoint list, traffic is still served.
</content>
</invoke>

thoughts.content: Found it: there are two frontend ReplicaSets — the old frontend-76d98597b9 (2 pods Running fine) and a new frontend-667786b9fd (1 pod, crash-looping with nginx BackOff). This confirms a recent rollout. Let me check the deployment spec, pod logs, and describe the failing pod.

Root cause mechanism confirmed in nginx startup logs: nginx: [emerg] unknown directive "proxy_conect_timeout" in /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf:9 — a typo in the config (missing "n" in "connect"). Let me verify the ConfigMap content and confirm this is the actual deployed config, then check if a previous good revision exists.

Root Cause: CONFIRMED

Alert: KubePodCrashLooping — frontend-667786b9fd-j5dnw in namespace shop, cluster aurora-lab

Evidence chain
Pod state (kubectl get pods -n shop): frontend-667786b9fd-j5dnw is 0/1 Error, 3 restarts in 65s. Two other frontend pods (frontend-76d98597b9-, old ReplicaSet) are 1/1 Running, 0 restarts.
Container logs (kubectl logs frontend-667786b9fd-j5dnw):
   ``
   2026/10/02 21:24:07 [emerg] 1#1: unknown directive "proxy_conect_timeout" in /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf:9
   nginx: [emerg] unknown directive "proxy_conect_timeout" in /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf:9
   `
   nginx fails to parse its config at startup and exits (Exit Code 1) — this is a fatal, deterministic failure, not resource/transient.
ConfigMap content (kubectl get configmap frontend-nginx -n shop -o yaml), line 9 of default.conf:
   `
   proxy_conect_timeout 2s;
   `
   Confirmed typo: proxy_conect_timeout is not a valid nginx directive (should be proxy_connect_timeout). This exactly matches the line/column nginx reported.
Why only one pod is crashing, not all frontends: kubectl get replicaset -n shop shows the new ReplicaSet frontend-667786b9fd carries annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt: 2026-10-02T17:23:27-04:00 — i.e. someone ran kubectl rollout restart deployment/frontend. This forced new pods to be created and mount the ConfigMap fresh. The old ReplicaSet's pods (frontend-76d98597b9-) have been running continuously since before the bad config was introduced — nginx doesn't hot-reload conf.d on its own, so their already-running master process never re-read the broken file. Summary

Root cause (CONFIRMED): The frontend-nginx ConfigMap in namespace shop has a typo on line 9 of default.conf: proxy_conect_timeout 2s; instead of proxy_connect_timeout 2s;. This is not a valid nginx directive, so nginx fails to start ([emerg] unknown directive, exit code 1), causing the pod frontend-667786b9fd-j5dnw to CrashLoopBackOff.

Why it only hit one pod: The new ReplicaSet was spawned by a kubectl rollout restart at 21:23:27 UTC. The 2 older frontend-76d98597b9-* pods were already running with the config loaded in memory before the ConfigMap was broken, and nginx doesn't hot-reload conf.d, so they kept serving fine — masking the problem until the restart created fresh pods that mounted the broken config for the first time.

Current impact: Partial degradation only — Service frontend endpoints still list the 2 healthy old pods, so traffic is being served. However, 1/3 desired replicas is unavailable, and there is currently no healthy "new" pod template to fall back on if the old pods are ever cycled.

Fix: Correct the typo in ConfigMap frontend-nginx (proxy_conect_timeout → proxy_connect_timeout), then kubectl rollout restart deployment/frontend to cycle pods onto the corrected config. Rolling back the Deployment revision would not fix this since the ConfigMap is referenced by plain name and shared across revisions.

Findings have been saved to memory for future reference on this pattern.
